findings.reason: this is wiring inside an already-specified function, not a design gap the plan's text should carry; the plan did the depth judgement (one query in one function) correctly.
findings.text: `refuse_protected_automatic_deletion` fabricates `[{"id": name, "status": "delete"}]` dicts solely to call `filter_protected(..., protected_names=set(protected_reasons))`, then reads back the returned `protected_ids`; `filter_protected` is documented to "strip protected editorial fields from approved items" and its loop is a set-membership test dressed as a field filter, so a deletion refusal is wired through a function whose contract is a different operation entirely. The membership answer is already `protected_reasons`' own keys, so the delegation adds a parallel path that a future change to the field-stripping semantics could silently alter.

findings.reason: §3 req 3 rules a ceiling onto "every automatic pass", so the plan should name `protection.py` as the single ceiling owner rather than leaving it to be duplicated per delete site.
findings.text: the plan's §3 requirement 3 asks for a volume ceiling on every automatic delete pass, but the ceiling exists only as `DERIVED_PARENT_CLEANUP_DELETION_LIMIT = 80`, a constant named for and enforced at one call site (`_delete_derived_parent_nodes`), while the shared owner of every deletion write — `deletion_change_cypher`/`deletion_change_params` in `provenance_lifecycle.py:148` — carries the recovery snapshot but no ceiling, and `protection.py`, which now owns `automatic_deletion_protections` and `filter_automatic_deletion_candidates`, owns no ceiling at all; extending a ceiling to a second automatic path therefore means minting a second site-specific constant. The owner to extend is `protection.py`, so the ceiling travels with the protection it bounds.

findings.reason: the section must state what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, before its surface is added.
findings.text: §4 (with §4a) adds interface surface: a new `sn restore` command group (`imas_codex/cli/sn.py:8545`) with `compose` and `apply` subcommands, a new public artifact definition `imas-codex.archive-reconstruction.v1` (`signed_manifest.py:185`, exercised at `sn.py:8371`), and a new refusal family (relationship type outside the registry, counterpart neither live nor included, a node already present with non-identical state, per-type archive-versus-live count mismatch). The section text names none of these as retiring or merging existing surface. Against this week's figures — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 — the addition is unaccounted.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the durable-authority query is one deep function: `automatic_deletion_protections(gc, name_ids)` at `protection.py:86` hides the whole spend/materialisation/publication-signal Cypher behind a single call returning an identity→reason map, and `deletion_change_cypher` at `provenance_lifecycle.py:148` hides the snapshot-plus-edge-inventory write behind one builder. Both hide more than they expose.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the volume ceiling is a per-site constant outside the module that now owns deletion protection.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds an `sn restore` command group, a new signed-artifact definition and a new refusal family without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searches the codebase before proposing machinery: §3 names `filter_protected` in `imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py` and reads its definition (correctly finding it matches `name_stage='approved'`, of which zero rows hold, so it returns the empty set); §4 is preceded by the restore reuse map (`docs/evidence/paid-identity-deletion-protection/restore-reuse-map.md`) that judged the archive-reconstruction adapter the one justified piece of new machinery; the deletion-recovery material is routed through the existing `deletion_change_cypher` builder in `provenance_lifecycle.py` rather than a parallel one.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `refuse_protected_automatic_deletion` reuses an editorial field-stripper as a set-membership predicate.
